title: Child Support and SNAP Recovery Orders Received from Issuing Agencies
content:
Terms on which the Department applies orders from the IV-D (child support) agency and the SNAP agency to benefit payments under Benefit Withholding and Deduction Orders. They govern the four agency kinds: Child Support Withholding — Current Support Order, Child Support Withholding — Arrears-Only Order, SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Household or Agency Error and SNAP Overissuance Recovery — Intentional Program Violation.

## Terms

**Term 1 — Mandatory once sent.** Child support and SNAP deductions are mandatory once the IV-D agency or the SNAP agency sends an order; the claimant cannot stop, suspend or change them, and disputes about the underlying debt are referred to the issuing agency.

**Term 2 — What an order must carry.** An agency order is recorded only when it carries an IV-D case number or SNAP claim number and, for arrears-only and SNAP orders, a certified total amount. Whether it carries them is read from the order as received and recorded by the Department, not from the claimant's account of it.

**Term 3 — Notice and start.** The claimant is mailed notice at least the kind's notice days (calendar days) before the first deduction, and the order applies to payments issued on or after the kind's effective lead business days after it is recorded; an amended order applies after the kind's amendment lead business days. An amendment changes the weekly amount or the certified amount. An order withdrawn by the issuing agency before it took effect is terminated.

**Term 4 — Suspension, resumption and termination.** An order is suspended or resumed only on the issuing agency's notice, and terminated on the agency's notice after the kind's termination lead business days or when its certified amount has been deducted in full. A suspended order may also be ended by the issuing agency, and is then terminated.

**Term 5 — Across claims.** Agency orders follow the claimant to payments on later claims and do not end when a claim closes; when a current support obligation ends, any remaining arrears are collected only under a separate arrears-only order.

**Term 6 — Payments reached.** Agency orders apply to payments under every program, including supplemental and reissued payments, but nothing is deducted for a waiting week or while no payment is issued.

## Acceptance of an order (Term 2 as a table)

| Kind | Reference number on the order | Certified total amount on the order | Recorded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current support order | Present | Not needed | Yes |
| Current support order | Missing | — | No |
| Arrears-only order | Present | Present | Yes |
| Arrears-only order | Present | Missing | No |
| Arrears-only order | Missing | — | No |
| SNAP order (either kind) | Present | Present | Yes |
| SNAP order (either kind) | Present | Missing | No |
| SNAP order (either kind) | Missing | — | No |

The reference number is the IV-D case number for a child support order and the SNAP claim number for a SNAP order.

## Who can change the status of an agency order

| Change | Made on |
|---|---|
| Suspend an active order | The issuing agency's notice only |
| Resume a suspended order | The issuing agency's notice only |
| Terminate an order | The issuing agency's notice (after the termination lead), or full deduction of the certified amount |
| Stop, suspend or change at the claimant's request | Not available to the claimant |

## Timing illustration (hypothetical)

*Dates and lead figures here are invented for illustration; the actual notice days and leads are the kind's own figures.* Suppose an order of a kind with a notice period of N calendar days and an effective lead of L business days is recorded on a given day. The first deduction can come only from a payment issued on or after the L-th business day after recording, and the claimant's notice is mailed at least N calendar days before that first deduction. If the order is later amended, the amended amount applies only after the kind's amendment lead, counted from the day the amendment is recorded.

## Across claims (hypothetical)

A claimant whose claim closes with an active SNAP Overissuance Recovery order later files a new claim: the order follows the claimant to payments on the new claim. A claimant whose current support obligation ends with arrears still owing: those arrears are collected only if a separate arrears-only order is received.
